figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Overview of gene replacement coupled with in vitro assembled RNP cleavage. (A) Replacement of pksP with an antibiotic resistance gene
by in vitro CRISPR coupled with dual Cas9 RNP cleavage. Dual crRNAs targeting the beginning and the end of pksP were assembled separately
with tracrRNAs to become sgRNAs. Two sgRNAs were then assembled with Cas9 to form the RNP. The repair template, consisting of a
phleomycin resistance gene (1477 bp), was amplified from plasmid pFC333. Wild-type A. wentii protoplasts were transformed with the RNPs
together with the repair template. (B) The pksP gene in A. wentii was replaced by the phleomycin selection marker through DNA cleavages induced
by the Cas9 RNP. The resulting white transformants, with the phleomycin resistance marker, were able to grow on media containing phleomycin.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Paired HPLC profiles of A. wentii (wild type, mcrAΔ, and mcrAΔ gedCΔ dual knockout strains) extracts when grown on a solid PDA
medium. (i) wild type, (ii) mcrAΔ, and (iii) mcrAΔ gedCΔ dual knockout strains. Compounds 1−15 are gedC-related, while compounds 16 and 17
are additional metabolites revealed in the dual knockout strain.

Figure 3. Chemical structures of the upregulated compounds in the A. wentii mcrAΔ strain. Emodin (1), physcion (2), sulochrin (3), physcion
bianthrone (4), 14-O-demethylsulochrin (5), (trans)-emodin bianthrone (6), (cis)-emodin bianthrone (7), (trans)-emodin physcion bianthrone
(8), (cis)-emodin physcion bianthrone (9).
